body:
## What

`SetFontMetrics` no longer asks the editor to scroll to the caret.

It returned `scroll_active=true`, so every font re-measure set `Main.scroll_to_caret`, and the next display revealed the caret. Re-measures happen:
- at load;
- again when web fonts settle (the `#font-specimen` size observer);
- on zoom.

None of these is the user moving the caret. A re-measure after the user had scrolled away jumped the editor back to the caret, and a click aimed below it landed on something else.

Startup still reveals the caret once on its own, because `scroll_to_caret` starts `true`.

## Measured

Headless Firefox, `dev`'s default page in a 420 px tall window. The test scrolls the editor to 501 px, leaving the caret (at 391 px) out of view, then resizes the font specimen as a web font loading does.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| scroll position after the re-measure (two runs each) | 362, caret back in view | 501, unchanged |

On the livelits branch (#2635), the same jump made a click on a livelit land on text: a click the instant the Shirt and Pants slide first drew its picture was lost 7–8 times in 8. With this change it lands 8 of 8. Details in [Hazel performance analysis, issue 001](http://matthewhammer.org/hazel/performance-analysis/001/) and hazelgrove/hazel#2609.

## Tests

The quick suite (4,318 tests) passes. The behaviour is a scroll in a real browser, so it was checked there rather than with a unit test.
